doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Trombonists, old string bands and dance steps
title: Tom called 'parlor music' because he read but did not fake
summary: Tom says players who could not read called him parlor music because he read well and could not fake. When music became popular, Isaiah Morgan, Chris Kelly and others came to him wanting to learn.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. He noticed all, but he couldn't, he wasn't sure he could count, you know. Yeah. The division, you know. He didn't show he could count. He, he come out and eat with me. I've been him playing it about four times. Yeah. And I told him, I said, you can go. But after he played, I know some of them fellas, you put them in them shop keys and four and five flats, they- Yeah. They could read it all right. Some of them, they couldn't read it, you understand. They had routine, I played all right. But they used to call me parlor music. Parlor music. Parlor music. Yeah. Everywhere I'd go they called me parlor music. So I used to go at the lake and play, they'd tell me, put on that parlor music, I need to make all music, you know. I wasn't much of a head. Didn't fake very much. No, I couldn't fake. But after a while everybody wanted to play music. Yeah. Coming around, Rene, they come home for this. Isaiah, Morgan, they come, only Sam, he didn't come. And Chris Kelly, I had them all come here to want music then. You see, music was getting popular then. Yeah. That head business, they couldn't, you know, they couldn't do that. Me with the parlor music, they all would follow me then. They used to kid me with the parlor music because I couldn't read them.
